newsitem.title: USA: Texaco to extract big returns from Monterey.
newsitem.headline: Texaco to extract big returns from Monterey.

text.p: Texaco Inc, already one of the top producers of heavy oil in California, is expected to pump up output and reduce production costs following its planned acquisition of Monterey Resources Inc.

The intergrated oil and natural gas giant has far better technoligical capabilities than the smaller independent player and is likely to generate much better returns for the properties, Wall Street analysts said.
"Texaco can add technological advancements that Monterey can't," said one investment banker.
Texaco earlier announced it would buy Monterey in a stock transaction valued at $21 per share, or nearly $1.2 billion. The deal also includes the assumption of $285 million in debt.

The deal comes just a few weeks after Santa Fe Energy spun off its 83 percent ownership stake in the independent producer. And in June, Monterey announced an agreement to buy McFarland Energy Inc for $106 million.
The transaction represents a significant premium to Monterey's current share price, which closed slightly above $15 on Friday. The stock jumped 5-3/16 to 20-1/4 in afternoon trading.

Although the price appears to be rich, Texaco is trading at extremely high multiples and can well afford to use its bouyant stock for the acquisition, said Bear Stearns & Co Inc analyst Fred Leuffer, who estimated the deal will be neutral to earnings and cash flow.
The transaction marks the latest move in a wave of consolidation amid independent oil and gas producers.
"Texaco already has critical mass in California. This is a core operation for them," said Michael Young of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Most of Texaco's current 126,000 barrel per day production in California is heavy crude.
Texaco did not disclose the estimated exchange ratio for the planned transaction or whether the deal includes any price protection mechanisms.
The move by Texaco comes amid industry rumors that it may be looking to buy Canadian heavy oil producer ELAN Energy Inc.
Texaco declined to comment on the speculation, but one of the company's top executives acknowledged that it would consider other acquisitions.

"We're looking for potentially other acquisitions in areas where we have a core business, proven core competencies and we see opportunities to expand," said Claire Farley, president of the company's North American production.
